## International research collaborations

| Institution | Country | Topics |
|---|---|---|
| Delft University of Technology, Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences | Netherlands | Long-term weathering effects on historic building materials and masonry quay walls; multiphase hygro-thermal modelling. |
| Institute for Sustainability and Innovation in Structural Engineering (ISISE) | Portugal | Moment-resisting timber connections, digital image correlation and numerical modelling. |
| ISISE | Portugal | BIM-supported data management for historical constructions, IoT workflows and low-cost LiDAR survey techniques. |
| Delft University of Technology, Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences | Netherlands | Damage between building components induced by seismic vibrations. |
| ISISE, University of Minho | Portugal | Experimental and numerical techniques, strengthening methods, masonry products and earthquake engineering. |
| Delft University of Technology, Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences | Netherlands | Full-scale masonry modelling and damaging block-based approaches for masonry structures. |
| University of California San Diego | United States | Locking-free displacement finite elements with nodal integration. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[34,18,48]"}

## Collaboration themes

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Heritage structures

Digital-twin workflows, survey-to-model pipelines, masonry diagnostics and
decision support for conservation.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Computational mechanics

Finite element and virtual element formulations, nonlinear response and robust
open-source implementation.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Sustainable materials

Bio-based and recycled materials, experimental characterization and numerical
modelling for building applications.
:::

:::
